title: A Mud Wall in the Desert Once Guarded All of China — Silk Road EP3 | China Travel Expert
description:
In the Gobi west of Dunhuang stands a crumbling block of rammed earth. Two thousand years ago, this mud wall was one of the gates in and out of the Chinese empire.

This is Yumen Pass — the "Jade Gate" — about 80 km northwest of Dunhuang in Gansu. Emperor Wu of Han erected it around 121 BC as a fortified checkpoint on the Hexi Corridor, and for centuries every Silk Road caravan on the northern route squeezed through it, trading jade and horses with Central Asia. It took its name from the jade caravans that passed through. Time has worn it down to a gatehouse, a beacon tower and a stretch of the tamped-earth Han Great Wall — and in 2014 it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the Silk Roads.

🧭 Expert Tip: Yumen Pass sits an easy day-trip from Dunhuang — pair it with the Mogao Caves and Crescent Lake so one Gansu base covers three Silk Road icons.
